course.title: Java Fundamentals: Control Flow, Methods and Arrays
course.description: Beginner course: decisions, loops, methods, recursion, arrays and strings.

lessons.title: if-else and switch
lessons.content: Use if, else if and else to run code conditionally. A switch statement chooses between many constant values, for example switch (day) { case 1 -> ...; default -> ... }. Always include a default case. Conditions must evaluate to a boolean; combine them with && and ||.
cards: Which keyword handles "otherwise" in a decision?
What must an if condition evaluate to?
When is switch better than if-else?
When comparing one variable against many constant values.

quiz.q: What type must an if condition have?
What does the default case in a switch do?
quiz.e: default handles every value not matched by a case.

lessons.title: Loops: for, while and do-while
lessons.content: A for loop repeats a block a known number of times: for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++). A while loop repeats while a condition is true, and do-while always runs its body at least once. The enhanced for (for (int x : arr)) walks arrays and collections. Update the loop variable or you get an infinite loop.
cards: Which loop always runs at least once?
Write a loop that runs 5 times.
A loop whose condition never becomes false.

quiz.q: Which loop checks its condition AFTER the body?
quiz.e: do-while evaluates the condition at the end.

quiz.q: for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) runs how many times?

lessons.title: break, continue and nested loops
lessons.content: break exits the nearest loop immediately; continue skips to the next iteration. Loops can be nested, for example a for inside a for to print a grid or a multiplication table. Labels such as outer: let break or continue target an outer loop.
cards: Exits the nearest enclosing loop (or switch) immediately.
Skips the rest of the current iteration and goes to the next one.
To process grids, tables and combinations (rows and columns).

quiz.q: Which statement skips to the next iteration?
quiz.e: continue jumps to the next iteration.

quiz.q: How many times does the inner body run in two nested loops of 3 and 4?

lessons.title: Methods and parameters
lessons.content: A method groups reusable code, for example static int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }. It has a return type (void if nothing is returned), a name and parameters. Java passes arguments by value: the method receives a copy of primitives and a copy of object references.
cards: What does the return type void mean?
Does Java pass arguments by value or by reference?
By value (object references are copied too).
To reuse code and keep programs organised.

quiz.q: Which keyword sends a value back from a method?
quiz.e: return gives the result to the caller.

quiz.q: A method with no result has return type...

lessons.title: Method overloading
lessons.content: Overloading means several methods share a name but have different parameter lists, such as print(int) and print(String). The compiler chooses the version from the argument types at compile time. Changing only the return type is not valid overloading.
cards: Same method name, different parameter lists.
When is the overloaded method chosen?
At compile time, from the argument types.
Is changing only the return type valid overloading?
No - the parameter list must differ.

quiz.e: Parameter types or count must differ.

lessons.title: Recursion
lessons.content: A recursive method calls itself with a smaller input until it reaches a base case, for example factorial(n) = n * factorial(n - 1) with factorial(0) = 1. Without a base case you get a StackOverflowError. Many recursive problems can also be solved with loops.
cards: The condition that stops the recursion.
What happens without a base case?

quiz.q: What error does infinite recursion cause?
quiz.e: The call stack runs out of space.

lessons.title: Arrays
lessons.content: An array stores a fixed number of elements of one type: int[] marks = new int[5]; or int[] a = {1, 2, 3};. Indexes start at 0 and arr.length gives the size. An invalid index throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Arrays.sort and Arrays.toString from java.util.Arrays are very handy.
cards: What is the first index of an array?
How do you get an array size?
What happens with an invalid index?

quiz.q: int[] a = new int[5]; the last valid index is...
Which expression gives the size of array a?

lessons.title: Two-dimensional arrays
lessons.content: A two-dimensional array is an array of arrays: int[][] grid = new int[3][4]; grid[1][2] = 7;. Use nested loops to process rows and columns. Rows can have different lengths (jagged arrays).
cards: How do you declare a 3x4 int grid?
How do you read row 1, column 2?
A 2D array whose rows have different lengths.

quiz.e: First index is the row, second the column (0-based).

quiz.q: Best way to visit every cell?
quiz.e: Use a loop over rows and one over columns.

lessons.title: String methods and StringBuilder
lessons.content: Strings are immutable. Useful methods: length(), charAt(i), substring(a, b), indexOf, equals, equalsIgnoreCase, toUpperCase, split and trim. Compare strings with equals, not ==. StringBuilder is a mutable buffer for efficient concatenation in loops: sb.append(x).reverse().toString().
cards: How do you compare two strings?
It builds strings efficiently without creating many objects.

quiz.e: A String cannot be changed after creation.

course.title: Java OOP Deep Dive and Exception Handling
course.description: Intermediate OOP: constructors, static/final, abstraction, interfaces, access control, enums and exceptions.

lessons.title: Constructors and the this keyword
lessons.content: A constructor initialises an object and can be overloaded. this refers to the current object and can call another constructor, for example this(name, 0). If you write no constructor Java supplies a default no-argument one, which disappears as soon as you define your own.
cards: When does Java provide a default constructor?
When the class declares no constructor.
How do you call another constructor?

quiz.e: Constructors never declare a return type.
It must be the first statement of the constructor.

lessons.title: static and final
lessons.content: static members belong to the class, not to individual objects, such as Math.max or a counter shared by all instances. final means unchangeable: a final variable is a constant, a final method cannot be overridden and a final class cannot be extended. Constants are usually static final in UPPER_CASE.
cards: The member belongs to the class, shared by all objects.
What does final mean on a variable?
Its value cannot change after assignment.

quiz.e: final classes (like String) cannot have subclasses.

lessons.title: Abstract classes
lessons.content: An abstract class cannot be instantiated and may contain abstract methods without a body that subclasses must implement. It can also have fields, constructors and normal methods. Use it when related classes share state and behaviour, for example abstract class Shape { abstract double area(); }.
cards: Can you create an object of an abstract class?
No, only of a concrete subclass.
A method declared without a body that subclasses must implement.
When subclasses share state and behaviour.

quiz.q: Which keyword declares a class that cannot be instantiated?
quiz.e: abstract classes are incomplete by design.

quiz.q: A concrete subclass of an abstract class must...
quiz.e: Otherwise it must also be abstract.

lessons.title: Interfaces
lessons.content: An interface declares a contract of methods that implementing classes must provide: class Dog implements Pet. A class can implement many interfaces. Since Java 8 interfaces can hold default and static methods. Use interfaces for capabilities such as Comparable and Runnable, and abstract classes for shared base code.
cards: Can a class implement several interfaces?
An interface method with a body (Java 8+).

lessons.title: Access modifiers and packages
lessons.content: private is visible only inside the class, default (no keyword) inside the package, protected inside the package and subclasses, public everywhere. Packages group related classes (package com.shop.model;) and avoid name clashes. Import classes with import java.util.List;.
cards: Which modifier is the most restrictive?
A namespace that groups related classes.

quiz.q: Which keyword brings a class from another package?

lessons.title: Enums
lessons.content: An enum defines a fixed set of constants: enum Day { MON, TUE, WED }. Enums can have fields, constructors and methods, and work well in switch statements. values() returns all constants and valueOf(String) converts text to an enum.
cards: A type with a fixed set of named constants.
An array of all enum constants.

quiz.q: Enum constants are usually written in...
Which method converts a String to an enum?

lessons.title: try, catch and finally
lessons.content: Exceptions are runtime problems such as dividing by zero. Wrap risky code in try, handle it in catch (ArithmeticException e) and put cleanup in finally, which always runs. Catch specific exceptions before general ones. try-with-resources closes AutoCloseable resources automatically.

quiz.q: Which block runs whether or not an exception occurs?

quiz.e: A general catch first would hide specific ones (compile error).

lessons.title: throw, throws and custom exceptions
lessons.content: throw raises an exception object; throws in a method signature declares a checked exception it may raise. Checked exceptions such as IOException must be handled or declared; unchecked ones (RuntimeException) need not be. Create your own with class InvalidAgeException extends Exception.
cards: throw raises an exception; throws declares one in the signature.
How to create a custom exception?

quiz.q: Which keyword declares possible exceptions in a method signature?

course.title: Java Collections, Generics and Streams
course.description: Intermediate: generics, sorting, queues, lambdas, the Streams API and Optional.

lessons.title: Generics
lessons.content: Generics let classes and methods work with any type while keeping type safety: List<String> names = new ArrayList<>(). You can write your own, such as class Box<T> { T value; }. Generics are checked at compile time and prevent ClassCastException. Primitives need wrapper types such as Integer.
cards: Compile-time type safety and no casting.
A type parameter (placeholder for a real type).

quiz.e: Generic type arguments must be reference types.

lessons.title: Comparable and Comparator
lessons.content: Comparable gives a class its natural order through compareTo(). Comparator defines an external order, for example list.sort(Comparator.comparing(Student::getMarks)). Collections.sort and TreeSet use these to order elements. compare returns a negative number, zero or a positive number.
cards: Comparable = natural order inside the class; Comparator = separate custom order.

quiz.q: To sort a list by a custom rule use...

lessons.title: Queue, Deque and Iterator
lessons.content: A Queue is first-in-first-out: offer() adds and poll() removes the head. A Deque such as ArrayDeque works at both ends and can act as a stack with push and pop. An Iterator walks any collection with hasNext() and next() and can safely remove elements with remove().
cards: Which class works as a stack?

quiz.q: Which method removes the head of a Queue?
quiz.e: poll() removes and returns the head.

lessons.title: Lambda expressions and functional interfaces
lessons.content: A lambda is a short anonymous function such as (a, b) -> a + b. It implements a functional interface, which has exactly one abstract method (Runnable, Comparator, Function, Predicate). Method references like String::toUpperCase make code even shorter.
cards: An interface with exactly one abstract method.

lessons.title: Streams API
lessons.content: A stream processes a collection in a pipeline: list.stream().filter(x -> x > 10).map(x -> x * 2).collect(Collectors.toList()). Intermediate operations (filter, map, sorted) are lazy; terminal operations (collect, forEach, count, sum) start the work. Streams do not modify the source collection.
cards: Does a stream change its source?

quiz.e: map applies a function to every element.
They run only when a terminal operation is called.

lessons.title: Optional
lessons.content: Optional<T> wraps a value that may be absent and helps avoid NullPointerException. Create one with Optional.of, ofNullable or empty. Use isPresent, orElse, orElseGet and ifPresent instead of null checks.
cards: To represent a missing value without null.
Create an Optional that may be null.

quiz.q: Which returns a default if empty?

course.title: Java Intermediate: File I/O, Threads and JDBC
course.description: Intermediate topics: files, serialization, multithreading, executors and database access with JDBC.

lessons.title: Reading and writing files
lessons.content: Use java.nio.file.Files for simple tasks: Files.readAllLines(path) and Files.writeString(path, text). For large files use BufferedReader and BufferedWriter inside try-with-resources. Always handle IOException.
cards: Easiest way to read all lines?
Which exception do file operations throw?

quiz.q: Which class buffers reading of text?

lessons.title: Serialization
lessons.content: Serialization converts an object to bytes so it can be saved or sent. The class must implement java.io.Serializable; ObjectOutputStream writes it and ObjectInputStream reads it back. Fields marked transient are skipped. Define serialVersionUID to control versioning.

quiz.q: Which keyword skips a field during serialization?

lessons.title: Threads and Runnable
lessons.content: A thread is an independent path of execution. Create one by implementing Runnable and passing it to new Thread(task).start(). Never call run() directly, because that does not start a new thread. join() waits for a thread to finish.
cards: How do you start a thread?
What does calling run() directly do?
Runs in the current thread - no new thread.

quiz.q: Which method starts a new thread?

lessons.title: Synchronization
lessons.content: When threads share mutable data you can get race conditions. The synchronized keyword lets only one thread at a time execute a method or block on the same lock. AtomicInteger and ConcurrentHashMap are thread-safe alternatives that need no explicit locks.
cards: Wrong results because threads access shared data at the same time.
Allows one thread at a time into the block/method.

quiz.e: Only one thread holds the lock.

lessons.title: ExecutorService
lessons.content: ExecutorService manages a pool of threads: ExecutorService ex = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4); ex.submit(task);. submit returns a Future whose get() waits for the result. Always call shutdown() when you are finished.
cards: What must you call at the end?

quiz.q: Which method waits for a task result?
quiz.e: get() blocks until the result is ready.

lessons.title: Connecting to a database with JDBC
lessons.content: JDBC is the standard Java API for relational databases. Add the driver, then DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, password) returns a Connection. Use try-with-resources so connections, statements and result sets are closed. Read a ResultSet with while (rs.next()).
cards: Java's standard API to access relational databases.
How do you get a connection?
How do you read result rows?

quiz.q: Which class opens a database connection?

quiz.e: It moves to the next row and returns a boolean.

lessons.title: PreparedStatement and CRUD
lessons.content: A PreparedStatement uses placeholders, for example INSERT INTO student(name, marks) VALUES (?, ?). Set values with setString and setInt, then call executeUpdate for INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE and executeQuery for SELECT. Prepared statements prevent SQL injection and are faster for repeated queries.
cards: It prevents SQL injection and can be reused efficiently.

quiz.q: What does ? represent in a PreparedStatement?
